text:
Ivy: quick heads-up 1 opened a PR to tighten the Reserved Capacity docs. Main things: clarify "burst" SLA language, add a tiny fallback example, and move runnable bits to /examples. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4502
Marco: nice. please call out which link was stale so we can add a redirect in the site config.
Ivy: migration guide had an old anchor (/legacy/terraform-migrate). proposing redirect to /migrate/terraform-and-cli and a short note about terragrunt differences.
Zara: on SLA phrasing, legal asked us to be explicit. suggest: "Reserved capacity is guaranteed; burst capacity has no SLA and may be routed to shared pools." short, contractual.
Rahul: agree. also add a one-line table showing fallbacks: Reserved pool -> Dedicated (if configured) -> Shared. That helps ops teams quickly scan.
Ivy: added that wording and a one-row table in the PR. also included a small example showing when spill happens: if reserved_utilization >= 100% and fallback.enabled = true -> spill to next tier.
Marco: for examples, can you split Terraform, CLI, and SDK into separate files under examples/reservations/ so reviewers can copy-paste? Putting code inline in the handbook makes it noisy.
Ivy: yes. moving them out. sample terraform I'll include: ```hcl
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "eng" {
  name = "eng-pool"
  gpus = 8
  isolation = "tenant" # allocation preference, not an absolute anti-eviction guarantee
}
```
Zara: please also include a short Python SDK example with idempotency guidance. customers retry and need to set a request id. e.g.: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(token=TOKEN)
client.reservations.create(name="ad-hoc", gpus=2, isolation="tenant", idempotency_key="req-42")
```
Rahul: can infra confirm the precise wording for "isolation"? customers interpret it as anti-eviction sometimes. We should add a single-sentence pointer to runtime/eviction-matrix.
Marco: infra confirmed in internal ticket: "tenant isolation biases allocation for the tenant but does not provide immunity from host-level preemption." Add that line and link to eviction-matrix.
Ivy: done. I added the one-line clarification and linked runtime/eviction-matrix. Also added a small priority note: reserved > dedicated > shared, with host-pressure override.
Zara: one more doc-style nit: consistently use "reserved pool" across the page, not "reserved capacity" or "tenant pool". I'll sweep for synonyms in the PR.
Ivy: good catch. I'll standardize language.
doc-bot: checklist created 1 move code samples to /examples/reservations/, update SLA wording to "burst has no SLA", add eviction-matrix link and one-line summary, add migration redirect, standardize "reserved pool" phrasing, include idempotency note in SDK examples.
Ivy: thanks everyone 1 will push the example split and request reviews from Marco + Zara. will ping when merged so Docs can backport to release-1.3.
Marco: leaving a small inline comment about fallback ordering phrasing 5 prefer arrow notation (Reserved -> Dedicated -> Shared) and a short sample scenario.
Zara: LGTM after those small edits.
Rahul: will review the example files once split. close when merged. :rocket:
